newsitem.title: USA: BPI Packaging exits t-shirt bag business.
newsitem.headline: BPI Packaging exits t-shirt bag business.

text.p: BPI Packaging Technologies Inc said Tuesday that it has exited the commodity plastic t-shirt bag business as of the end of it fiscal year ended February 28, 1997.
The company said it has taken reserves and write-offs of $7,397,000, the majority of which were for this product line.
BPI reported a loss of $0.97 a share, including this charge, for the 1997 fiscal year, compared to a loss of $0.38 a share the year before.

"By eliminating the drag of accelerating losses in commodity plastic t-shirt bags, we forecast that fiscal 1998 sales will be greater than fiscal 1997 and that the company will be profitable," the company said in a press release.

The company said that additional costs of the restructuring will impact the first quarter of Fiscal 1998, ended May 30, 1997, and these additional costs will not be fully offset by year-end reserves in the quarter.
However, the company said it expects to show a profit in the second quarter due to growing proprietary bag and film sales, reserves and cost reductions.

The restructuring has resulted in the company reducing its work force 26 percent and reducing salary, wages, fringe benefit costs and other variable costs by an estimated $6.0 million annually, it said.
